mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies / competent corporate registry in the parent entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) if issued in a Hague Apostille Convention state, notarize the certificate where required and then obtain an apostille from the designated competent authority of that state; (B) if issued in a non-Convention state, notarize, authenticate through the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction. Never use both paths on the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or corporate registrar in the parent entity's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Hague Apostille member state: notarization (if required) followed by apostille from the competent authority; (B) Non-member state: notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and then consular legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the parent entity authorizing the incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa and the filing of UBO disclosures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity board of directors / company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) if originating in an Apostille Convention state, execute before a notary and then apostille; (B) if originating in a non-Convention state, execute before a notary, have the document authenticated by the competent foreign ministry, and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Do not apply apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Korean formation agent / local counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity as principal, executed before a notary public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Hague Apostille Convention state: notarization followed by apostille from the designated competent authority; (B) non-Convention state: notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and consular legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction. These are alternative routes; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / constitutional documents of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the parent entity's jurisdiction or certified issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Apostille Convention state: notarize or certify, then apostille; (B) non-Convention state: notarize or certify, authenticate through the issuing state's foreign ministry, then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Use one path exclusively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the parent entity's banking relationship and account history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal bank of the parent entity, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) if issued in an Apostille Convention state, the bank signature must be notarized and then covered by an apostille from the competent authority; (B) if issued in a non-Convention state, the notarized bank letter must be authenticated by the issuing state's foreign ministry and then legalized by the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any foreign shareholder subscribes for shares in the Chusik Hoesa, all natural persons owning 25% or more, all board members, and all authorized signatories must be identified. Formation counsel must run a negative news and sanctions search against the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. BIS Entity List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, and domestic watchlists published by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). Korean law requires enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates, and any positive hit or unexplained source-of-wealth red flag must be resolved before filing; if unresolved, a Suspicious Transaction Report must be considered and incorporation counsel must decline the mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registry Service (I-RO / Internet Deunggi So) at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean Commercial Act Articles 19 and 20, a Chusik Hoesa trade name must be written in Hangul and must end with the statutory suffix 주식회사. The name should follow a four-tier conformity review: (1) distinctive Hangul name element; (2) accurate business object description; (3) optional Romanized or foreign transliteration used only as a secondary name; and (4) mandatory corporate form suffix at the end. Identical names in the same registration district for the same business object are refused, and misleading names that falsely suggest government affiliation, financial licensing, or unrelated business objects are not registrable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration officer rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written objection with supporting corrections to the senior registration officer of the same district court within two weeks of the rejection notice. If that objection is dismissed, the applicant may file an immediate appeal (즉시항고) to the trial division of the district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act, and a further appeal (재항고) to the Supreme Court may be available for a legal error. An existing name reservation cannot be extended after expiry; the applicant must file a new reservation before the 180-day window closes, and any rejected name should be corrected to remove the prohibited or confusing element before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not acceptable for this digital-health app entity for Korean tax and banking purposes. The National Tax Service requires an actual business place (실질적 사업장) with a signed lease in the company's name, a visible corporate sign, utility records, and evidence of operational substance; banks will also conduct site visits and UBO interviews before opening an account. A licensed serviced office with a dedicated physical workstation and contracted administrative support may be accepted provisionally, but Apple IAP / Google Play Billing revenue attribution and VAT registration issues make a virtual mail-only address highly risky. A physical registered office in an office-commercial zone of Seoul or Seongnam is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced on-site inspection: (i) exterior signboard displaying the registered trade name; (ii) dedicated lease agreement in the company's name with proof of deposit; (iii) working office desk, computer, and IT/server records; (iv) utility, internet, and telephone bills issued at the registered address; (v) payroll, contractor, or board-meeting documents showing use of the address; (vi) corporate seal and statutory records maintained at the address; (vii) banking records consistent with declared operations. Quantified risk: for a standard-risk digital-health app with a dedicated serviced office, estimated probability of an on-site inspection within the first 24 months is 15-20%; if a pure virtual office, residential address, or commercial-mailbox address is used, the probability exceeds 65% and tax registration may be revoked.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 18365, as amended), Articles 288-317, 369 and 383-393; specifically Article 292 (notarization of Articles of Incorporation), Article 295 (payment of subscription price), and Article 317 (registration of incorporation); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 4-5; Registration Office practices under the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registration Division having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office. For a Seoul-registered entity, the competent office is the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division (Seoul Central District Court Registration Office).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Corporation (Bup-in Seol-lip Deung-gi Sinhcheong), together with a certified notarized copy of the Articles of Incorporation and all statutory annexes required by the Korean Commercial Act and court registration regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act; the promoters may fix the capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation. Nonetheless, the entire issue price of all subscribed shares must be fully paid into a domestic foreign-exchange bank before incorporation registration, and the bank's certificate of deposit of the subscription price must be produced to the court. No government blocked escrow account is required; the domestic bank capital account serves as a restricted deposit until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] CO., LTD. (CHUSIK HOESA), REPUBLIC OF KOREA

WHEREAS [●] Co., Ltd. has been incorporated as a stock corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and

WHEREAS the Company's Articles of Incorporation have been subscribed, executed and notarized in accordance with Article 292 of the Commercial Act; and

WHEREAS the entire issue price of the initial ordinary shares has been fully subscribed and paid into [●] Bank in the Republic of Korea, and the bank's certificate of deposit of the subscription price has been obtained; and

WHEREAS the first Board of Directors is required to organize the Company and to adopt the foundational governance and administrative resolutions necessary for the commencement of the Company's digital health and fitness telemetry application business; and

WHEREAS the Company intends to operate the statutory corporate seat, bank accounts, and executive management in a manner compliant with the Commercial Act, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and all applicable financial and tax regulations.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The Board ratifies the subscription and issuance of [●] ordinary shares for a total paid-in capital of KRW [●]. The Board confirms that the subscribed issue price has been fully paid in cash and that no share has been issued below par value. The Board directs the issuance of share certificates and the preparation of the shareholder register in accordance with the Commercial Act.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the opening, maintenance and operation of demand deposit and settlement accounts with [●] Bank and other domestic financial institutions. The Board designates [●] as Representative Director, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, and [●] as second authorized signatory, and adopts a dual-signature mandate for all payments above KRW [●]. The Board further authorizes the corporate seal to be used for banking applications and directs that all account documents be filed with the respective banks.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts the registered office located at [●], Republic of Korea, as the Company's statutory seat for all legal, tax and regulatory purposes. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to execute or ratify a lease agreement for the premises, to register the office with the District Court Registry and the National Tax Service, and to notify the relevant authorities of any future relocation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public licensed in the Republic of Korea, together with licensed Korean corporate counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage qualified Korean corporate counsel and a notary public in the court district of the intended registered office. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, precise purpose clauses for digital fitness tracking, mobile health application development and telemetry services, authorized share capital, share classes, board composition, accounting period, and registered office address. The promoters must execute the Articles, and the notary must certify the document because an unnotarized Articles of Incorporation is invalid under Article 292 of the Commercial Act. The final text must be consistent with the ISIC 6201 digital health app business and must not contain irrelevant physical manufacturing or warehousing purposes.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identification copies of all promoters
Residential address verification for each promoter
Foreigner registration card, if already available
Corporate name searching or name reservation confirmation
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Written consent of all initial subscribers to the Articles
Power of attorney appointing legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing counsel identifies a defect, cure the defect by amending the purpose clause or capital clause and re-executing the Articles with a new execution date. Any false, vague or unlawful purpose language must be corrected before notarization; a second notarization may be necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Inward Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA (Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency) or a designated Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before remitting share subscription funds into Korea, non-resident investors must file a Foreign Investment Report through KOTRA's Invest Korea platform or the designated foreign exchange bank through which the capital will be remitted. The report must identify each foreign investor, the amount of foreign investment, the proposed corporate name, and the business purpose of establishing a Chusik Hoesa for digital health and fitness application services. KOTRA or the bank will issue the foreign investment certificate or official receipt that serves as evidence of permitted inward remittance. After receipt, the investor may remit the capital in accordance with the report. This step is an absolute prerequisite for non-resident ownership and foreign capital registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report application form
Passport or corporate identity documents of foreign investors
Power of attorney for filing
Bank account opening forms for the foreign exchange bank
Statement of source of funds
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the report is returned for correction, amend the investment amount or investor identity details and resubmit the corrected report immediately. Keep all banking remittance receipts and foreign exchange transaction confirmations because these documents are later required for the court registration and tax filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Full Payment of Subscription Price and Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic Foreign Exchange Bank where the pre-registration capital collection account is maintained.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-registration capital collection account in accordance with Korean commercial registration and foreign exchange practice. Deposit the entire subscription price in Korean won into the restricted account and obtain the bank's certificate of deposit of the subscription price. The certificate must identify the Company in formation as the intended depositor, the total deposit amount, the account number, and the exact date of deposit. The certificate is indispensable evidence of compliance with Articles 290 and 295 of the Commercial Act and must be attached to the court incorporation application. The deposit remains restricted until the court accepts the incorporation registration, after which the account can be converted into the Company's ordinary operating account.
required_dossiers: Pre-registration capital account opening application
Foreign exchange remittance confirmation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or identification of signatories
Foreign Investment Report certificate, if applicable
Bank certificate of deposit of subscription price
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money-laundering or know-your-customer documentation, deliver the requested documents within two business days. If the remitted amount differs from the nominal share capital due to foreign-exchange conversion, obtain the bank's official exchange-rate confirmation and reconcile the share subscription statement accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Incorporation Registration of the Chusik Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial District Court Registration Division; for Seoul-registered offices, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Corporation with the competent district court registration division. Attach the certified copy of notarized Articles, the bank certificate of subscription price deposit, the written consent of each director and auditor, the representative director's signature specimen, and the corporate seal registration application. The registration division will verify the legality of the company name, object clauses, share capital evidence, number of directors, and notarization. Once the court accepts the application, the Company is registered, obtains the corporation registration number, and acquires legal personality. No separate industrial operating license is required for this stage.
required_dossiers: Court registration application form
Certified copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of subscription price deposit
Consent to accept office executed by each director and auditor
Specimen signature and corporate seal card of the representative director
Application for company seal registration
Proof of payment of court filing fee and local registration license tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary instruction, file the requested correction within the court's stated period, normally seven days. If registration is denied, promptly rectify the legal defects and file an objection with the court within the statutory two-week period or submit a new corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Corporate Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the Commissioner of the National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after court incorporation, file for corporate business registration at the NTS tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The filing registers the Company for value-added tax, corporate income tax, and the issuance of electronic tax invoices. Submit the court-issued certificate of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, notarized Articles, lease agreement, and identification of the representative director. The NTS will issue the corporate registration number and business registration certificate. This certificate is required before the Company can reliably invoice clients, receive Google Play Billing and Apple IAP proceeds through Korean accounts, or comply with the digital app revenue reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration from the court
Corporate seal certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease agreement and landlord occupancy documents
Business registration application form
Identification of representative director
Corporate information questionnaire for tax purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the registered office lease or representative director identity, cure the issue by submitting a revised lease, a letter of consent from the landlord, or a foreigner registration certificate. If business registration is suspended, support the application with corrected evidence and seek administrative review through the NTS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Social Insurance and Foreign-Invested Company Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Employment Insurance Service (KEIS), National Health Insurance Service, and KOTRA for foreign-invested company post-filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, register the Company for national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance if the Company will hire employees. File the Foreign-Invested Company report with KOTRA or the designated administrative authority within the statutory period after business registration and capital remittance. Open permanent operating bank accounts with the domestic bank and convert the pre-registration capital account into a normal corporate account. Appoint a domestic privacy representative if the fitness app will collect or process personal biometric data under the Personal Information Protection Act. These obligations are operational legal compliance, not industrial licensing requirements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
National Tax Service business registration certificate
Employment contract or first employee registration forms
Foreign-Invested Company report form
Corporate bank account opening forms
Employee insurance enrollment forms
Privacy policy or data protection governance documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KEIS reports a data mismatch, file an amended registration form. If KOTRA challenges the foreign investment report, submit supplemental investor or corporate documentation. If the bank refuses to release the restricted capital account, provide the certified business registration and corporate certificate and cooperate with the bank's compliance team.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The registered business is pure digital software and mobile application development under ISIC 6201 and does not involve a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No factory establishment permit, small-scale manufacturing declaration, or industrial license under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act is required for the fitness and health telemetry app development company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea; Not Applicable to a non-manufacturing digital software activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The Company's proposed activity is outside the mandatory and voluntary EIA threshold categories under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act because it involves no physical construction, industrial discharge, or land-use change.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The operation generates no industrial wastewater discharge, fixed-source air pollutants, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste streams attributable to software development and cloud-based telemetry processing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; official electronic portal HomeTax at www.hometax.go.kr; administrative filing is made through the local District Tax Office for the entity's registered business address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean Chusik Hoesa obtains its Tax Identification Number by filing a Business Registration Application with the competent NTS District Tax Office within 20 calendar days from commencement of business. Required attachments include the certificate of incorporation and corporate registration, articles of incorporation, proof of the registered office, shareholder and director identification, and Korean bank account details. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number that serves as the unified TIN for Corporate Income Tax, VAT, and withholding tax purposes. A foreign entity without a Korean establishment that supplies digital services to Korean users may separately apply for simplified VAT registration through HomeTax and must appoint a domestic tax representative where direct filing is not administratively feasible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Korea has no US-style check-the-box election. A Chusik Hoesa is a statutory resident corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through election is available. Eligible domestic corporate groups may elect consolidated corporate income tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules disallow deductions for payments treated as not includible by the counterparty jurisdiction. For VAT, a business with annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000 may be classified as a simplified taxpayer for filing purposes, but this does not alter entity-level corporate income taxation. Foreign tax credit elections for direct and indirect foreign taxes are available under the applicable tax treaty and domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for VAT registration; any person commencing a business activity in Korea must register for VAT within 20 days of commencement. A simplified taxpayer filing regime applies to individual businesses with annual gross turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but the entity remains a registered VAT taxpayer and must charge 10% VAT on taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all registered corporate taxpayers through the NTS HomeTax system. The e-Tax Invoice must be transmitted to the NTS and communicated to the buyer by no later than the day following the issuance date. Korea does not require physical fiscal stamping; the NTS issues a digital acceptance and validation number upon electronic receipt. NTS-certified e-invoicing providers use API integrations, ERP interfaces, or HomeTax web services for submission. Failure to issue or transmit an electronic tax invoice triggers a penalty tax of 1% of the supply value, plus general late-payment interest. Cash receipts are mandatory for qualifying final-consumption sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies to goods physically exported from Korea and to services supplied to non-resident customers outside Korea, including digital health and fitness application subscriptions, biometric telemetry, wellness tracking platforms, and hosted analytics delivered to foreign end users. The Korean supplier must hold a valid Business Registration Number, issue an electronic export tax invoice, and maintain evidence that the place of supply is outside Korea. For app-store distribution, sales to Korean resident consumers remain standard-rated at 10% VAT despite the App Store or Google Play commission interface; sales to non-resident foreign consumers qualify for zero-rating when the contract, foreign-currency payment, and offshore consumption evidence are complete.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (mandatory for physical goods; for pure digital services, the equivalent controlled record is the e-Tax export invoice and export service register filed with the VAT refund claim)

Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export movement for goods; for digital fitness app exports, the equivalent is the online platform download/usage log and App Store sales report showing foreign end-user access
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank MT103, or foreign-currency collection confirmation evidencing payment from the foreign purchaser
International service, subscription, or licensing agreement identifying the foreign counterparty, product scope, contract value, and delivery terms
Country-of-use, IP geolocation, and telemetry usage logs substantiating that the health fitness app services are consumed outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are closely audited by the NTS and Korea Customs Service. Auditors compare export declarations, e-Tax invoices, foreign-currency receipts, contract counterparties, and digital consumption logs. If export proceeds are not collected in foreign currency within 180 days, the zero-rating is retroactively reversed, 10% VAT is assessed, and input VAT credits are clawed back. Fraudulent or fictitious export claims, including circular financing, fabricated download logs, or sham foreign buyers, attract an additional tax surcharge of up to 40% of the over-refunded or evaded VAT, daily overdue interest, a 10-year extended statute of limitations, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) is the central bank authority, acting as the principal foreign exchange information and settlement oversight institution together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF). Routine foreign exchange transactions and corporate banking operations are delegated to licensed foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and its Enforcement Decree and Foreign Exchange Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains liberalized current account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Cross-border receipts from digital subscription services, app store payouts, royalties, and operating revenue settlements are generally freely convertible and remittable, subject to foreign exchange transaction reporting through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are also permitted but are subject to registration or reporting requirements. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is structurally available to non-resident shareholders of a Chusik Hoesa, but the remitting Korean company must demonstrate: (i) distributable profits from carefully prepared financial statements; (ii) a valid shareholders meeting or sole-shareholder distribution resolution; (iii) compliance with Korean dividend withholding tax at the applicable statutory rate, generally 20% plus 2% resident surcharge, or a lower rate under an applicable tax treaty; (iv) settlement of the tax withholding through the Tax Number of the non-resident shareholder; and (v) presentation of the corresponding tax payment certificate and foreign exchange purpose documentation to the Korean foreign exchange bank. There is no general requirement to obtain a separate central bank license or permit for a standard dividend remittance once the underlying tax and foreign exchange reporting obligations are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and the Korean Foreign Exchange Regulations, export proceeds must be received within the statutory settlement timeline, generally 15 months from the date of export or service performance for goods and digitally delivered services unless the Korean foreign exchange bank approves a clearly documented extension. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero: South Korea does not currently require surrender of export receipts, and the Chusik Hoesa may retain 100% of export proceeds in a multi-currency foreign exchange account at a licensed Korean bank. If proceeds are not received by the settlement deadline, the company and the bank must file the required foreign exchange change report to MOEF/BOK, and the unreceived amounts may be reclassified as a capital transaction rather than a current account export collection. For Apple App Store and Google Play subscription revenue, the qualifying evidence consists of the platform financial statements, payout statements, merchant remittance reports, tax invoices supplied by the platform, and a copy of the platform distribution agreement demonstrating the true recipient of the digital service revenue.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail and high legal constraint. A foreign electronic money institution or offshore digital EMI, such as a non-Korean licensed neobank or payment wallet operator, cannot serve as the Chusik Hoesa statutory Korean foreign exchange bank for FETA settlement, inbound foreign investment reporting, dividend remittance, or KRW clearing. Such EMIs may be used only as ancillary collection and payout gateways for non-Korean expenses and vendor payments. The Korean Chusik Hoesa must maintain its central treasury, KRW liquidity, and foreign exchange compliance accounts with a Korean-licensed commercial bank, while an EMI can be used for low-value operational disbursements only where no KRW settlement or Korean regulatory reporting obligation is triggered.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for new corporate account opening in South Korea. At least one director or the sole director, or a duly authorized signatory on the record, must attend an in-person KYC interview at the chosen Korean bank branch. Pure remote onboarding is not standard for a newly formed foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, and banks will normally reject a remote-only model for non-resident UBOs and directors. If the director cannot travel, the bank may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney executed in favor of a resident Korean-based authorized signatory, but the final risk decision rests with the bank's compliance committee. The physical visit should occur before the inbound capital remittance is sent, and the original passports, corporate registration certificate, company seal certificate if applicable, articles of incorporation, shareholder registry, and UBO declarations must be presented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App store revenue received from Apple and Google rather than from direct B2B customer invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program Agreement; Google Play Distribution Agreement; App Store Connect financial reports; monthly payout statements from Apple and Google; commission tax invoices; user subscription analytics; operational revenue reconciliation report; and a board-approved transfer pricing and revenue recognition policy for digital subscription sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to contractors and technology vendors in multiple overseas jurisdictions create correspondent banking scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved vendor whitelist; executed service agreements; itemized invoices; source-of-funds evidence; payment schedule aligning with the cash-flow forecast; sanctions and PEP screening policy; and a documented AML risk assessment for the receiving jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern over foreign-source funds used for the initial capital injection into the Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of shareholder bank statements showing accumulation of capital; personal or corporate tax returns of the investor; liquidation or exit transaction documents if the funds came from a previous business; a signed source-of-funds declaration; and certified copies of contracts, share sale deeds, or inheritance documents as applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee director or indirect ownership concerns in the Korean corporate registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of no nominee arrangement; notarized declaration by the registered director that he or she is the de facto manager; share capital contribution receipts; bank confirmation of the identity of the wired investor; and a resolution of the shareholders approving the management role of the registered director.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank as the receiving bank. If the capital injection is made by a non-resident in exchange for newly issued shares, the investor or the company must first file a foreign investment report with the Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before the inbound remittance. After receipt, the bank will issue a certificate of foreign investment and the company must file the share issuance and any director/shareholder changes with the Korean court registry. The compliant wire is an SWIFT MT103 addressed to the beneficiary bank BIC with the exact legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, the KRW or USD account number, the beneficiary address in Korea, and the remittance purpose stated as foreign direct investment for subscription of shares. On the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System the transaction must be classified as an inward capital transaction with the purpose code for foreign direct investment equity acquisition, not as a current account trade payment. Verification requires the investor's passport, certificate of incorporation from the home jurisdiction, apostilled corporate docs, source-of-funds evidence, a board resolution authorizing the share issuance, and the foreign investment report confirmation from the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rail for cross-border trade settlement is SWIFT MT103 for the transfer of USD, EUR, or other foreign currency from the Korean bank account to the beneficiary bank. Commercial letters of credit are not necessary for digital subscription services, but an irrevocable at-sight commercial LC can be used for physical procurement such as hardware or promotional merchandise. For ordinary operating disbursements, the company should use the Korean bank electronic cash management system to make local KRW vendor payments, and SWIFT MT103 international payment orders for overseas vendors. Each cross-border outbound payment requires a foreign exchange purpose classification, underlying documentary evidence such as a contract or invoice, and a valid tax invoice or withholding tax payment proof where Korean withholding tax applies. The Apple and Google app store settlement proceeds are received net of commission into the company's foreign currency account; those balances should be swept regularly to the Korean multi-currency treasury account and converted to KRW through the bank's corporate FX desk or a permissible hedging instrument.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts executed with a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank under the real-demand hedging rule
KRW/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDF) only where the bank confirms legal availability for a resident company hedging demonstrable underlying export subscription exposure
Cross-currency swaps converting USD or EUR revenue streams into KRW for term liquidity and capital financing needs
Plain-vanilla FX options and collar structures to protect budget exchange rates without creating speculative open positions
Multi-currency cash pooling and natural hedging via same-day matching of USD/EUR receipts and disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with attached financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities by March 31 of the following year, with one-month extension available if prepared and filed by a certified tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid or underreported corporate tax, or 5% when no tax is due, plus an overdue daily surcharge of approximately 0.022% on the unpaid tax; the NTS may conduct estimated assessment, levy seizure and collection enforcement, and revoke the business registration for a permanently non-compliant or dormant entity. No administrative strike-off exists under Korean law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular Annual General Meeting of Shareholders for approval of annual financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book (no external filing; obligation prescribed by the Korean Commercial Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December fiscal year-end, by March 31. Courts may permit extension only in exceptional, unavoidable circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting exposes responsible directors to administrative fines under the Commercial Act and civil liability for damages caused to shareholders. The failure does not by itself lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and audited financial statements, if the compulsory external audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART system or external audit reporting portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements and the audit report must be submitted to the FSS within two weeks after the external auditor issues the report, and in any event by the date of the regular shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to obtain a mandatory external audit results in administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and may invalidate the shareholders' approval of financial statements; for egregious non-compliance, the FSS may designate an auditor or require corrective measures. There is no automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and audit of statutory corporate registers and minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate registered office (register inspection by shareholders, creditors, and court or administrative authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance; update upon each share transfer, director change, and meeting; no separate annual government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal to permit inspection or incomplete statutory registers subjects the company and managing directors to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; incorrect registers may also block shareholders' exercise of rights and expose the company to damages claims. No strike-off consequence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to external audit if its fiscal year-end total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9 million. Listed companies and enterprises designated as public-interest companies under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies are subject to external audit regardless of asset size. Companies below the threshold are not statutorily required to appoint an independent auditor but may do so voluntarily.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are required for listed and public-interest companies; other entities may elect K-IFRS or the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP). The accounting framework chosen must be consistently applied and must be sufficient for NTS corporate tax return preparation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing for a private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is evidenced by the register of members and share certificates; every share transfer must be recorded in the register of members before it becomes effective against the company. For anti-money-laundering purposes, banks and licensed financial institutions apply real-name verification under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act at account opening, and the company must maintain adequate UBO data for tax and foreign-investment reporting where applicable. There is no annual shareholding confirmation return to a central corporate registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors or audit committee members, if applicable
Minute Book for shareholders' meetings and directors' meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory progressive corporate tax rates range from 9% to 24% on the national tax base, plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing an effective headline rate of 27.5%. No general statutory tax holiday applies to digital health app companies. Eligible R&D expenditures under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act may claim tax credits of up to 40% for qualifying SME R&D. Tax loss carryforward limited to 5 years, with no carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate tax returns are filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax system. The principal forms are the Corporate Tax Return for the Tax Base and Tax Amount Computation (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서) and the Local Income Tax Return filed via WeTax, the local tax e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate tax returns must be filed within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year. For a December year-end, the statutory deadline is March 31. Interim and preliminary returns are also filed semi-annually by corporations with prior-year taxable income exceeding prescribed thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and fiscal year-period details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Korean permanent establishment must register a domestic business identification number and file a final return under the domestic corporate tax identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of comprehensive income and reconciliation of accounting profit to tax basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches must reconcile Korean-source income and provide a full trial balance and tax adjustment schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of tax adjustments, including temporary and permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-entity adjustments must follow Korean tax accounting rules; intercompany app development and IP cost allocations require a transfer pricing schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of taxable income (loss) after adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must preserve simultaneous documentation proving app subscription and IAP commissions are attributable to a local fixed place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of tax rates, progressive brackets and local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch profits are taxed at the same corporate rate and an additional branch remittance tax under the tax treaty may apply to repatriated branch profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deductions, including R&D credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must be substantiated with tax authority certificates and treaty limitation computations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties accrue at 0.03% per day of the unpaid tax amount, capped at 10% of the tax due. Underreporting penalties are 10% of the understated tax. Unfiled returns attract an additional 20% penalty. The National Tax Service may impose additional penalties of up to 40% for false or fraudulent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is granted upon submission of a Certificate of Residency (COE/TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a Korea Application for Tax Exemption/Reduction (Form 20), and supporting beneficial ownership documents. The withholding agent applies the treaty rate only after NTS confirmation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 22% statutory (20% + 2% local); treaty reduction varies (e.g. 10% or 15%). Interest: 22% statutory; treaty rates generally 10% or 15%. Cross-border app IP royalty and intra-group licensing must satisfy the OECD transfer pricing principles and beneficial ownership requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Total cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion trigger mandatory Local File and Master File submission; a threshold of KRW 100 billion triggers full contemporaneous documentation retention.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Korean Chusik Hoesa entities are subject to domestic and OECD economic substance standards; no-true-substance overseas outsourcing of core revenue functions may be recharacterised and trigger anti-shell-company and substance disallowance penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Inflated Royalty Remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties to a related offshore entity for standard app code that has no substantive IP development in Korea, effectively stripping Korean-source profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length result, addition of 10-40% penalties on underreported income, and a 20% withholding penalty on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the shortfall if the company becomes insolvent, and face criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining minimal substance while deriving substantial digital health app revenue from Korean consumers, including director-only boards and subcontracting core development to a tax-haven affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and disallowance of intercompany deductions; 40% fraud penalties; referral for criminal investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in operating the shell may be personally disqualified, prosecuted for tax fraud, and exposed to civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing subscription payments through unapproved payment rails or obscure offshore merchant accounts contrary to the App Store/Google Play payment policies and Korean Electronic Financial Transactions Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties, business suspensions, and criminal fines for operating an unlicensed payment aggregation or money transmission business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined and imprisoned for violations of Korean AML and electronic financial transaction regulations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Consistently missing the 3-month annual filing deadline and failing to withhold or remit dividend, interest, or royalty taxes due to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 0.03% daily late payment surcharge; 10% understatement penalty; interest and additional 20% non-filing penalty; suspension of tax clearance certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for the unpaid corporate tax plus penalties when acts are grossly negligent or intentional.
